data.long_meaning: A name derived from Sanskrit, meaning 'beyond' or 'past'. In Hindu mythology, Apurva can refer to the eternal and immutable nature of the divine. It is a powerful and evocative name, resonating with the depth and complexity of the Hindu spiritual tradition. The name Apurba carries the meaning “Beyond, Past” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Sanskrit tradition and is also used in Hindi, Sanskrit, Marathi. Parents who choose Apurba usually hope their child will grow to embody beyond, past and live with faith, good character and purpose.

Apurva is often used to describe something that transcends the boundaries of time and space, and is therefore beyond the reach of mortal perception or comprehension. In this sense, the name carries a sense of awe and reverence, inspiring us to look beyond the mundane reality of life and connect with the deeper, spiritual dimensions of existence.

historical_references.reference: Apurba was an early medieval Bengali poet, born around 1150 AD. He is considered one of the pioneers of the Bengali Bhakti movement and is renowned for his devotional poetry dedicated to Lord Shiva. His most famous work, the 'Apurba Samhita', is a collection of hymns and stories about the god.
historical_references.context: Bengali Bhakti movement and devotional poetry to Lord Shiva

historical_references.reference: Apurba was also a prominent figure in the medieval Tantra tradition in Bengal. He is believed to have been a guru (teacher) to many Tantric masters and is known for his contributions to the development of the Bengali Tantra tradition. His works include the 'Apurba Tantra', which is a significant text in this tradition.
